strategy_desc: Framed as studying acquired drug resistance — what mutations reduce inhibitor binding?

parsed_mutations.rationale: Isoleucine to valine substitution at position 82 (I82V) reduces binding affinity for inhibitors by altering hydrophobic interactions within the active site, while maintaining catalytic activity due to minimal structural disruption.

Valine to alanine substitution at position 84 (V84A) decreases the size of the side chain, which can reduce van der Waals interactions with inhibitors but retains sufficient flexibility and activity for substrate binding.

Methionine to leucine substitution at position 46 (M46L) modifies the shape of the binding pocket, reducing inhibitor affinity while preserving enzymatic function due to the structural similarity of leucine and methionine.

Isoleucine to methionine substitution at position 90 (I90M) introduces a larger sulfur-containing side chain, which can interfere with inhibitor binding but maintains catalytic activity by preserving the overall fold of the protein.

Glycine to alanine substitution at position 47 (G47A) introduces a slightly bulkier side chain that can hinder inhibitor binding without significantly disrupting the flexibility needed for substrate processing.

target_meta.clinical_context: Drug target for multiple FDA-approved protease inhibitors (Saquinavir, Ritonavir)
